ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $BC=4\text{cm}$. A point $E$ is chosen on $AC$ such that $EC=BC$. A line $EF$ is drawn perpendicular to $AC$, and $CF$ is connected so that $CF=AB$. If $EF=10\text{cm}$, what is the length of $AE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $EF\perp AC$,\\
it follows that $\angle CEF = \angle ACB = 90^\circ$,\\
In right $\triangle ACB$ and right $\triangle FEC$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
AB = FC \\
BC = CE
\end{array}\right.$,\\
hence, right $\triangle ACB \cong$ right $\triangle FEC$,\\
thus, AC = $EF = 10\text{cm}$, EC = $BC = 4\text{cm}$,\\
hence, AE = AC - EC = $\boxed{6\text{cm}}$,

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure there is a vertical line segment, point A is above, point C is below, and point E is located between A and C, so A, E, and C are on the same straight line; from E it is connected to F to the right, and EF is perpendicular to AC; the figure also draws triangle ABC and the connecting line CF, and the two right triangles involved are △ABC and △FEC. Reasoning: It is known that ∠ACB=90°, and EF⊥AC, so ∠CEF=90°. In right △ACB and right △FEC, AB and FC are respectively the hypotenuses, and the problem gives CF=AB; at the same time EC=BC, and BC=4 cm. Thus the two right triangles have “equal hypotenuses and one equal right side,” so by the HL criterion it can be obtained that △ACB≅△FEC. Corresponding sides are equal, so AC=EF=10 cm. Also because E is on AC, EC=BC=4 cm, therefore AE=AC−EC=10−4=6 cm.
